title: Ezekiel 17:22–24
context: The LORD now speaks of what he himself will do. He will take a tender twig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain of Israel, where it will become a noble cedar sheltering birds of every kind. All the trees of the field will know that the LORD brings down and exalts. Both traditions read the passage as a hope image for the house of David, in line with the promise of 2 Samuel 7, and many Christian readers in both see its fulfillment in the Messiah, linking it with Isaiah 11:1 and Jeremiah 23:5.

verses.text: “The Lord GOD says: ‘I will also take some of the lofty top of the cedar, and will plant it. I will crop off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
verses.arminianNotes: I will also take some of the lofty top of the cedar, and will plant it. Arminian readers see the LORD himself acting where human kings failed, planting a tender twig on a high mountain.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the deliberate echo of 17:3-4: what the eagle did in conquest, the LORD will do in grace. The image is commonly read as the restoration of David’s line, in keeping with 2 Samuel 7:13.

verses.text: I will plant it in the mountain of the height of Israel; and it will produce boughs, and bear fruit, and be a good cedar. Birds of every kind will dwell in the shade of its branches.
verses.arminianNotes: I will plant it in the mountain of the height of Israel; Arminian readers see a hope of restoration in which the cedar bears fruit and offers shelter to birds of every kind.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that many Christian readers in both traditions see here the Messiah and a kingdom that gathers many; some compare Matthew 13:32, while others are more cautious about the link.

verses.text: All the trees of the field will know that I, the LORD, have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree flourish. “ ‘I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: All the trees of the field will know that I, the LORD, have brought down the high tree, Arminian readers see the LORD’s rule over the nations: he brings down the proud and raises the lowly.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see shared ground in the LORD abasing and exalting, compare 1 Samuel 2:7 and Luke 1:52. The closing words, I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it, stress certainty.
